Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to offer users a way to migrate their data and settings from an existing app to a designated replacement app. Here are the details.

iOS to Make App Replacements Easier

Although it's an uncommon situation, developers sometimes retire an existing app and launch a new one to replace it, asking users to move to a separate standalone app.

While most developers work hard to make the transition as smooth as possible, the migration process can still require some effort on the user's part — especially when data not stored in the cloud is involved.

With iOS 27.2, Apple addresses this issue with a new system-managed migration flow that can move the data and supported settings of an app over to a designated replacement app before the original one is deleted.

Based on code currently found in iOS 27.2 beta 1, users will see a prompt reading:

"The developer suggests that your existing "%1$@" app data and settings be migrated to the new "%2$@" app. Your iPhone can do this for you now, before you start using the new app. Afterwards, the old app will be deleted from this iPhone."

Users can then choose either "Migrate App Data & Settings" or "Don't Migrate Anything." If a user declines the migration, iOS will show a second confirmation warning, noting that some preferences — including notifications and location settings — may need to be reconfigured.

It's worth clarifying that this functionality appears to be limited to developers replacing their own apps with a designated successor, rather than migrating data between apps from different developers.

Based on the current implementation, iOS can migrate a range of system-level settings and permissions, including:

  • Privacy, Location, and Health authorization decisions
  • Notification settings, including accessory notification settings
  • Per-app Do Not Disturb and Focus settings
  • App Lock and Protection settings
  • CarPlay icon arrangement and compatible widget layouts
  • Live Activities and Accessory Live Activities
  • Access to relevant accessories
  • LaunchServices preferences, fonts, capture-related defaults, phone data, and Secure Element services

We'll be keeping a close eye on any changes to this framework during the iOS 27.2 beta testing period, and will report back as we learn more about how developers implement this functionality.
